newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate falls 80 bps to 9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate falls 80 bps to 9 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate fell 80 basis points to 9.0 percent on Monday due to strong bank liquidity and a higher volume of call money borrowings.
Daily settlements totalled 58.3 million kuna against the supply of 100 million and dealers said liquidity remained pretty high ahead of fortnightly reserve payments.
Fresh deals amounted to 42.9 million kuna most of which were call money loans at an unchanged 8.0 percent.

Banks rolled over previous loans at rates ranging between 8.0 percent for call money and 18 percent for two-month funds, while insurers charged 8.0 for old call money and 14 percent for one-month funds.
A central bank official said banks had 6.75 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, up from 2.5 million on Friday.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Tuesday slightly weaker at 6.4012 from 6.4008 against the dollar and firmer at 3.5681 from 3.5693 versus the German mark.
